introduction:
A Registered Will is a pivotal legal instrument that ensures your assets and properties are distributed precisely according to your final wishes. By formally registering the Will under the Indian Registration Act, 1908, you provide it with an undisputed legal backing, significantly minimizing the chances of future familial disputes or fraudulent claims in Uttar Pradesh.

Registration ensures the document is safely preserved in the official government custody (Book No. 3), providing an authentic reference that cannot be easily tampered with, destroyed, or forged.
quickFacts:
Important Quick Facts
  • Is Registration Mandatory? No, it is optional but highly recommended to avoid future disputes and prove authenticity in court.
  • Validity: A registered Will is valid for a lifetime unless you make a new one (which automatically supersedes the old one).
  • Cost: Nominal fixed registration fee (typically approx. ₹100–₹500). There is no stamp duty on Wills.
  • Processing Time: The process at the Sub-Registrar Office usually takes about 1-2 hours; the registered document is often returned the same day or within a few days.
  • Location: Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) in your district (Tehsil).
documentsRequired:
Documents Required for Will Registration

Note: You must carry the original and one set of self-attested photocopies of all documents to the Sub-Registrar Office.
For the Testator (Will Maker)
  • Original Will: Typed or handwritten on plain paper (Stamp paper is not required, but acceptable if used).
  • Identity Proof: Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, or Passport.
  • Address Proof: Aadhaar Card, Voter ID, or Driving License.
  • Photographs: Two passport-size color photos.
  • Medical Certificate: (Highly Recommended) A certificate from a registered doctor stating you are of "sound mind," especially if you are a senior citizen (70+), to prevent future claims of mental instability.
For the Two Witnesses
  • Identity & Address Proof: Aadhaar Card or Voter ID for both witnesses.
  • Photographs: One passport-size photo for each witness.
  • Witness Guideline: Witnesses should be reliable people who are preferably younger than the testator and must not be beneficiaries in the Will.
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Online Pre-Registration & Slot Booking

Important Update (2026): Walk-in registrations are no longer allowed. You must book a 1-hour appointment slot online before visiting the office.
Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Step 1 (Visit the Portal): Go to the official IGRSUP portal (igrsup.gov.in).
  2. Step 2 (Register/Login): Click on "Property Registration" (संपत्ति पंजीकरण) -> "Apply Here" (आवेदन करें). Even though it says "Property," this portal section handles all deed and Will registrations. Create a login ID if you are a new user.
  3. Step 3 (Start New Application): Select your District, Tehsil, and Sub-Registrar Office (SRO). Under the Deed Type / Nature of Document, select "Will" or "Vasiyat".
  4. Step 4 (Fill Details): Enter the complete demographic details of the Testator and the two Witnesses.
  5. Step 5 (Pay Fees): Pay the nominal registration fee online via the integrated gateway, or generate the offline challan/receipt to pay at the bank/counter.
  6. Step 6 (Book Appointment Slot): Select an available date and pick a specific 1-hour time slot from the calendar.
  7. Step 7 (Print Acknowledgement): Download and print the Appointment Slip, the payment confirmation receipt, and the application summary.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Physical Visit to the Sub-Registrar Office (SRO)

The physical visit to the SRO is mandatory to verify the identity of the testator and execute the registration under Book No. 3.

Step-by-Step SRO Process:
  1. Step 1 (Arrive Early): Reach the SRO at least 15 minutes before your booked 1-hour slot. Late arrivals will miss the slot and require a complete re-booking.
  2. Step 2 (Document Verification): Present your printed Appointment Slip, online summary form, Original Will, Medical Fitness Certificate, and original IDs to the SRO clerk.
  3. Step 3 (Biometric Capture): The registration officer will verify you and capture thumb impressions, fingerprints, and live photos of you (the Testator) and your two witnesses.
  4. Step 4 (Signing & Execution): You (the Testator) and both witnesses will physically sign the registry book and the Will pages in the direct presence of the Sub-Registrar.
  5. Step 5 (Scanning): The Sub-Registrar will scan the executed Will to store a permanent digital copy in the government database.
afterApplying:
After Applying — Custody & Certified Copies

1. Original Will Collection

The original physical Will is returned to the Testator immediately after the Sub-Registrar's scanning and endorsement. It will feature a registration number and SRO seal on the back.

2. Certified Copy (CC)

The government safely archives the scanned copy. If the original Will is ever lost, destroyed, or damaged, the legal heirs can apply for and obtain a Certified Copy (CC) from the SRO. This copy is fully admissible in court.

3. Safekeeping & Disclosure

Store the original registered Will in a secure location (e.g., a bank locker). Ensure you inform the appointed Executor or a highly trusted family member of its exact storage location.
